title: Setting Up Redis
description: Install Redis locally with Docker, configure persistence and security, and connect a C# or Node.js application for local development.

data.text: Getting Redis running locally takes minutes with Docker, but a proper setup includes persistence, password protection, and network isolation. This lesson walks you through a developer-friendly Redis installation you can safely reuse across projects.
Docker avoids OS-specific package issues and makes it easy to reset state. The official Redis image is lightweight, and you can mount a host directory for persistent data.

data.title: docker-compose.yml for Redis
data.content: Define a Redis service with a password and volume for persistence.
data.code:
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data
    command: redis-server --requirepass redispass --appendonly yes

volumes:
  redis-data:

data.title: Never run without a password locally
data.text: Always set requirepass even on localhost. This prevents accidental exposure if you later expose ports to the network or share screenshots with open terminals.

Redis ships with a conservative default configuration. For development, the most important settings are memory caps, persistence mode, and protected mode. You can override any setting in redis.conf or pass flags on startup.

data.title: redis.conf essentials
data.content: Enable AOF persistence, set a password, and cap memory.
data.code:
bind 127.0.0.1
protected-mode yes
requirepass redispass
maxmemory 512mb
maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
appendonly yes
appendfsync everysec

data.text: Both StackExchange.Redis and ioredis accept a password through connection configuration. Verify the connection with a simple PING before running application code.

data.caption: Local Redis development setup flow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Install Docker] --> B[docker compose up -d]
    B --> C[redis-cli ping]
    C --> D[Set password / maxmemory]
    D --> E[Connect from app]
    E --> F{App connects?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Run tests]
    F -->|No| H[Check firewall / port / password]
    H --> E

data.title: Post-installation checklist
items: Run `redis-cli INFO server` to confirm the version and port.
Run `redis-cli INFO persistence` to verify AOF is active.
Connect from your application and run a test SET / GET.

items.question: Should I use Redis on Windows without Docker?
items.answer: Redis is Linux-native. The old Windows ports are no longer maintained. Use Docker or WSL2 for a supported local environment.

items.question: What port does Redis use by default?
items.answer: Redis listens on TCP 6379 by default. Change it in redis.conf or via the --port flag if another service already occupies that port.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Docker is the fastest way to run a consistent local Redis instance.
Always set a password, maxmemory, and persistence in development.
Verify connectivity from redis-cli before wiring up application code.
